investigacion.base:
Here's where things stand on day 2 of the conference (20 Oct 2026). Based on what I could find, nothing points to YES yet. The plenary hasn't closed, and no reports of serious deadlock have surfaced.

**What the resolution sources say**
- **ENB/IISD page:** My search didn't return the ENB page itself. ENB is covering the conference, though: its photos appear in reports from the opening, including one of CBD Executive Secretary Astrid Schomaker credited to IISD/ENB – Mike Muzurakis. I couldn't read any daily bulletins.
- **CBD site:** It says the UN 2026 Biodiversity Conference, including COP17, CP-MOP12 and NP-MOP6, will take place from 19 to 30 October 2026 in Yerevan. I saw nothing about a suspension, which you'd expect this early.
- **Metaculus "credible sources":** This is just a definition (major news outlets and official bodies). I didn't pull the page.

**Latest news**
- 16 Oct: Armenia hosted a Leaders' Summit before the opening. IUCN pushed for a credible and action-oriented Yerevan package that responds directly to the implementation barriers identified across all 23 targets.
- 18–19 Oct: The opening ceremony was held on Sunday, 18 October, and COP17 formally began on October 19, 2026… More than 10,000 delegates have gathered in the city. The COP President is Hambardzum Matevosyan, Armenia's environment minister.
- **Main agenda:** The "Yerevan Pathway"—a program of concrete steps to accelerate implementation, which grows out of the first global review of the framework. Context: countries are currently not on track to meet 22 out of the framework's 23 targets. The likely fights are over inadequate financing, limited technical capacity, gaps in scientific co-operation.
- **Side controversy:** Armenia approved the Amulsar gold mine (despite years of environmental and human rights concerns). This is a reputational issue for the host and isn't likely to affect the procedural outcome.
- **Tracker:** Carbon Brief is running a live table showing how close countries are to consensus on each text (tracking the progress of countries towards consensus on dozens of negotiating texts). It's useful for watching late in week two.

**Base rates (from my own knowledge, not checked in this search)**
- COP16 in Cali (2024) was suspended after running into overtime. Delegates left, the meeting lost quorum, and the finance and resource mobilization decisions plus the budget were left unadopted. A resumed session in Rome in February 2025 finished the agenda.
- COP15 part 1 (Kunming, 2021) was split into two parts on purpose because of COVID. That's a different situation.
- COP15 part 2 (Montreal, 2022), COP14 (2018), COP13 (2016) and earlier COPs mostly closed late, sometimes after midnight, but did finish their agendas.
- So unplanned suspension of a CBD COP is rare: roughly 1 out of the last ~8 regular COPs. Running past the scheduled close is very common, and under the question's rules that still counts as NO.
- **Specific risks this time:** Resource mobilization and the financial mechanism are still contentious after the Rome compromise. The budget and the core programme of work have to be adopted. Quorum can be lost if the meeting runs very late on 30–31 October, since delegates have flights to catch. That is exactly what happened in Cali.

**Upcoming dates**
- High-level segment: probably in the second week (exact dates not confirmed in my search).
- Scheduled close: 30 Oct.
- Cutoff for resolution: 23:59 Yerevan time on 31 Oct.

**Prediction markets:** I didn't find any.

**Status if it resolved today:** NO, because there's no suspension. The real test is the closing plenary on 30–31 October.

criterios:
This question resolves YES if the seventeenth meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD COP17), held in Yerevan, Armenia (19–30 October 2026), is formally suspended by its President at the closing plenary with one or more substantive (non-procedural) agenda decisions left unadopted — such that a resumed session is required to complete the agenda, mirroring what occurred at COP16 in Cali in November 2024. It resolves NO if the closing plenary instead concludes/closes the meeting with the agenda completed (even if the plenary runs past midnight into 31 October 2026 Yerevan time).

Resolution will be based on the IISD Earth Negotiations Bulletin daily coverage of the conference ([enb.iisd.org/un-biodiversity-conference-cbd-cop17](https://enb.iisd.org/un-biodiversity-conference-cbd-cop17)) and/or official CBD announcements ([cbd.int/conferences/2026](https://www.cbd.int/conferences/2026)), or [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). Specifically, if these sources report that the COP17 closing plenary was "suspended" (as opposed to "closed"/"concluded") with decisions pending, the question resolves YES.
letra_pequena: Only the status of the COP17 plenary itself matters; the status of the concurrent Cartagena Protocol (CP-MOP 12) and Nagoya Protocol (NP-MOP 6) meetings is not considered. A meeting that runs past its scheduled 30 October closing date into the early hours of 31 October (or slightly later) but then formally closes with its agenda completed resolves NO. If the conference has not formally closed or been suspended by the time of resolution because the plenary is still ongoing, the question resolves based on the status reported by the sources as of 23:59 Yerevan time on 31 October 2026. If the CBD and IISD sources become permanently unavailable, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) will be used.
razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** About 10 days until the scheduled close on 30 October; the resolution cutoff is late on 31 October, Yerevan time.

(b) **Status quo:** COP17 is underway, with no reported deadlock or suspension. That is not yet a resolved NO.

(c) **Reference class:** The supplied history suggests roughly 1 unplanned suspension among the last 8 regular CBD COPs—an approximate 12% base rate.

(d) **NO scenario:** Delegates compromise on finance and other contested texts, then formally close COP17 with its agenda completed, even if the plenary runs late.

(e) **YES scenario:** Finance negotiations delay the final plenary until it loses quorum; the President formally suspends COP17 with substantive decisions unadopted, requiring a resumed session.

(f) **Technicality:** Running past 30 October does not count. The criterion requires a *formal suspension of COP17 itself*, with substantive decisions pending—not merely an overtime plenary or a suspension of a concurrent protocol meeting.

The recent Cali precedent and recurring finance disputes raise the risk somewhat above the rough base rate, but there is no evidence yet of the specific breakdown needed for YES.

Probability: 16%

(a) **Time left:** COP17 is scheduled to close in 10 days, on 30 October. The resolution cutoff is 23:59 Yerevan time on 31 October.

(b) **Status quo:** Negotiations are ongoing, with no reported deadlock pointing to a suspension. If they proceed normally, the outcome is NO.

(c) **Reference class:** The research summary identifies one unplanned suspension among roughly the last eight regular CBD COPs—a base rate of about 12%.

(d) **NO scenario:** Delegates reach compromises on finance and the global review, adopt the remaining decisions, and formally close COP17, even if the plenary runs late.

(e) **YES scenario:** A substantive dispute delays the final plenary until delegates leave, quorum is lost, and the President formally suspends COP17 with decisions still pending.

(f) **Technicality:** Running past 30 October does **not** count as YES. The suspension must concern the **COP17 plenary itself**, leave at least one substantive decision unadopted, and require a resumed session; the concurrent protocol meetings do not count.

The Cali precedent and finance disputes raise the risk, but an unplanned suspension remains unusual. With no specific sign of an impasse yet, I put the probability modestly above the historical base rate.

Probability: 15%

**(a) Time left:** The closing plenary is scheduled for 30 October 2026. The outcome should be known by 31 October, roughly 10–11 days from now.

**(b) Status quo:** The conference has just opened. There is no suspension and no reported deadlock, and the default path for CBD COPs is a late but formal close. If nothing changed, this resolves NO.

**(c) Reference class and base rate:** Regular CBD COPs from roughly COP9 (Bonn 2008) to COP16 (Cali 2024).
- Nagoya, Hyderabad, Pyeongchang, Cancún, Sharm el-Sheikh and Montreal all closed, often after midnight.
- Kunming's split was planned in advance because of COVID, so it doesn't count.
- Cali is the only unplanned suspension for loss of quorum.

That gives a base rate of about 1 in 8–10, or roughly 10–12%.

Adjustments:
- **Pushing down:** After the Cali embarrassment, the Secretariat and Bureau will be alert to quorum risk and to managing time. The finance fight was partly defused by the Rome roadmap, which deferred the decision on a permanent finance arrangement to later COPs.
- **Pushing up:** Finance and resource mobilisation, the 2027–28 budget, and the global review outcome ("Yerevan Pathway") are all contentious. Armenia is a less experienced presidency. Ten thousand delegates with flights booked for 30–31 October recreates Cali's quorum risk.

**(d) NO scenario:** Negotiations run late. The presidency pushes contested finance and review texts through with bracketed compromises in an overnight plenary, and gavels the meeting closed in the early hours of 31 October with the budget and all decisions adopted.

**(e) YES scenario:** Finance or resource mobilisation stays deadlocked into 31 October. Delegations, especially smaller developing-country ones, leave for flights, and quorum is challenged or lost. The President suspends the meeting with the budget or finance decisions pending, and a resumed session (online or in 2027) is needed.

**(f) Technicalities:**
- Only a formal "suspension" with substantive decisions unadopted counts. Running late and then closing is NO.
- If the plenary is still ongoing at 23:59 on 31 October, resolution is based on the status reported then. An unfinished but unsuspended plenary would most likely be read as not suspended.
- A procedural suspension later resolved by closure counts as NO.
- The Cartagena and Nagoya protocol meetings are excluded.

Probability: 9%
